text.p: Here are the highlights from Swiss newspapers on Thusday:
- Switzerland will join Nato's Partnership for Peace, the Swiss government decided on Wednesday.

- Arthur Liener, the Swiss army chief of staff, submitted his resignation. A parlamentary commission will publish a report on the so-called 'Nyffenegger scandal' in two weeks. Insiders believe that that the report will incriminate Liener.
- Swiss Finance Minister Kaspar Villiger plans to cut the salary sum of the public sector by one percent.

- Former CEO of Credit Swiss Josef Ackermann has been appointed member of the executive board at Deutsche Bank, where he will be responsible for credit controls, treasury and macroeconomics. - Swiss electro group Landis & Gyr said that it will close down a production plant in Berlin. Some 70 jobs will go.
- Swiss ambassador to the United States Carlo Jagmetti warned at a media conference in Washington against 'hasty conclusions' with regard to Nazi gold. He also citicized the press.

- Several hundred employees of the Huerlimann and Cardinal breweries in Zurich and Fribourg protested against the decision of parent group Feldschloesschen to shut the two breweries. -- Zurich Editorial +41 1 631 7340
